title: When the LLM Wiki Meets Linked Data: Local Agent Memory That Scales
description:
Tony Seale’s starting point is the pattern Andrej Karpathy calls the "LLM wiki": a folder of markdown notes that an agent can read and write. AI builders love it for its simplicity, but it struggles at enterprise scale because notes capture what happened without capturing what it means, and the agent has to rebuild that meaning every time.

Tony's answer borrows from the way JSON-LD brought machine-readable meaning to the web. Treat the YAML front matter of each note as linked data against a shared context, and a folder of markdown becomes a knowledge graph that people can still read and edit as normal.

In this session, he will:
demonstrate the approach live on a single markdown note
introduce the open Vault-LD specification
share what a year of running an AI-native business this way has taught him, including why every class in an ontology has a cost

A session for anyone building agents who have hit the limits of file-based memory, and for ontologists working out where their skills fit in agentic AI.
